title: Shark Attacks
text:
The Global Shark Attack File (GSAF) is a record of shark incidents around the world, kept by investigators who log where each one happened, what the person was doing, and how it ended. This site uses a cleaned version of that file covering 5,094 incidents from 1900 onward.
Sharks have a fearsome reputation, but the data tell a calmer story. Only 943 of these incidents, about 18.5 percent, were fatal, and that is across more than a century and the whole world. Attacks have grown more common over time, but that rise follows the boom in surfing, swimming, and beach travel rather than more dangerous water. More people in the ocean means more chances for an encounter, not more aggressive sharks.
Use the navbar to explore the analysis. The Map page shows which countries report the most attacks, and the Trends page shows how attacks changed by year and which activities carry the most risk.
